user_message: A heavier object has more gravitational force on it, so it must fall faster than a light object even in a vacuum. Where does this reasoning fail?
allowed_evidence: Near Earth, gravitational force is approximately F_g=m_g g. Newton's second law is F=m_i a. Experiments show that gravitational and inertial mass are proportional; in conventional units they are numerically equal. In a vacuum, air resistance is absent.
public_rubric: Pinpoints the cancellation between greater force and greater inertia.
Derives the common acceleration from the supplied equations and the equivalence of gravitational and inertial mass.
Separates vacuum behavior from air-resistance effects.
States an appropriate approximation or limitation.
